# Centipede appears in the plain scenes column instead of ENEMIES (AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66)

## Problem statement

The dedicated `GymCentipede` enemy gym scene is discovered by the generic `Gym<Name>`
glob in `GymIndex` and rendered in the left-hand **plain scenes** column. The
Centipede is an enemy archetype, so it belongs in the middle **ENEMIES** column —
exactly where the analogous `GymBoss` scene already lives — so the index no longer
miscategorises an enemy testbed as a general-purpose scene.

## Users

- **Developer browsing the gym index** — expects enemy gym scenes to be grouped in the
  ENEMIES column so an enemy testbed is launched from the correct section.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear in the **ENEMIES** column so that
  every enemy testbed is grouped together on the index.
- As a **developer**, I want `GymCentipede` to appear exactly once on the index (in the
  ENEMIES column, not the plain-scene column) so I don't see a confusing, miscategorised
  entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — `GymCentipede` removed from the plain scenes column:** `GymIndex.listedScenes`
      no longer contains `GymCentipede` and no `Centipede` text row is rendered at the
      plain-scenes column X (`GAME_WIDTH * GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X.scenes`).
- [ ] **AC2 — No separate `Centipede` entry on the gym index:** `GymIndex.listedEnemyScenes`
      contains exactly `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]` — no dedicated `Centipede` row — and
      `GymCentipede` is not listed in any index column (per the producer's review decision:
      "it should appear in the dropdown in the enemies gym", not as a separate entry).
- [ ] **AC3 — The `Centipede` enemy type appears in the in-panel dropdown of the enemies
      gym:** `GymFodderEnemies`'s enemy selector (`enemy-gym-select`) lists a `Centipede`
      option (label `Centipede`), alongside the discovered non-boss `EnemyConfig`s, and
      seeding `init({ enemyKey: 'centipede' })` works.
- [ ] **AC4 — Selecting `Centipede` in the enemies gym runs the shared linked chain:** the
      scene rebuilds via the *same* `CentipedeChain` / `Centipede` code `PlayScene` and
      `GymCentipede` run (`src/scenes/gym/core/centipedeFormation.ts`): one `Centipede`
      segment per `CENTIPEDE_SEGMENT_COUNT`, a shared chain, and the config-tuning controls
      hidden (the Centipede has no CSV row to tune or save). Switching back to a config
      archetype restores the config-driven formation and the tuning controls.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests:** `GymIndex.test.ts` drops the dedicated-row expectations; new
      assertions cover the dropdown `Centipede` option (presence, label, chain build,
      control hiding, round-trip back to a config). Every existing test continues to pass.
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code
      comments, `README.md`, and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the three-column layout and the existing column X positions (`GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X`)
  unchanged; this is a categorisation change only.
- Mirror the existing `GymBoss` exclusion/surfacing pattern in `GymIndex.ts`; do **not**
  introduce a new generic "auto-route every enemy gym to ENEMIES" mechanism (scope creep —
  see Risks).
- No behavioural change to `GymCentipede` itself (only its index visibility/labelling).
- Do **not** modify `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` — it stays a pure discovery helper; the
  column categorisation is owned by `GymIndex`.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` builds `this.entries` from
  `discoverGymScenes(loadGymSceneModules())`, filtering out `GymFodderEnemies`, `GymBoss`
  and the Dev Utilities set (`DEV_UTILITY_SCENE_KEYS`). `GymCentipede` is **not** filtered,
  so it falls through into the left plain-scenes column.
- `this.enemyEntries` is currently hard-coded to `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCentipede.test.ts` asserts chain parity only; it does not assert index
  listing, so it needs no change.
- The Centipede is a **wave opt-in** (`centipede: true` in `PlayScene`), not a CSV enemy
  config, so it is not part of the `GymFodderEnemies` dropdown roster.

## Desired change (revised per producer review)

The producer's manual review (2026-10-14) rejected the dedicated-ENEMIES-row approach:
*"It appears in the enemies column now, but as a separate entry, it should appear in the
dropdown in the enemies gym."* The Centipede is an enemy archetype, so it should be
selectable **inside** the reusable enemies gym (`GymFodderEnemies`) rather than occupying a
separate index row (and it must stay out of the plain-scenes column).

1. Keep `GymCentipede` excluded from the plain-scenes list in `GymIndex.ts`.
2. Remove the dedicated `Centipede` ENEMIES row (`this.enemyEntries` reverts to
   `[Fodder Enemies, Boss]`).
3. Surface the Centipede as a dedicated option in `GymFodderEnemies`'s in-panel enemy
   selector (`enemy-gym-select`): selecting it (or deep-linking
   `init({ enemyKey: 'centipede' })`) swaps the scene to the **shared** centipede chain
   formation. The chain code is owned once in
   `src/scenes/gym/core/centipedeFormation.ts` and consumed by both `GymCentipede` and
   `GymFodderEnemies`, so game/gym parity holds by construction.
4. While the Centipede is active, hide the config-tuning controls (`#enemy-gym-config-body`):
   it is a wave opt-in, not a CSV row, so there is nothing to tune or save.
5. Update the module/class doc comments that enumerate the column exclusions, README and
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`. Do **not** modify `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`
   (pure discovery helper) or add a generic auto-route mechanism for every enemy scene.

## Key Files
## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/centipedeFormation.ts` — (new) the single shared Centipede chain
  formation config + per-scene chain registry, consumed by `GymCentipede` and
  `GymFodderEnemies`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymCentipede.ts` — thin wrapper over the shared module (unchanged public
  API).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — add the `Centipede` option to the enemy selector;
  branch `init`/`_selectEnemy` to the shared centipede formation; hide `#enemy-gym-config-body`
  while the Centipede is active.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — keep `GymCentipede` excluded from the plain scenes; remove the
  dedicated ENEMIES row; update column doc comments.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — updated and
  new assertions as per AC5.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §Gym surface / §8.5: record that the Centipede
  is surfaced in the enemies-gym dropdown, excluded from the plain scene list and not a
  separate ENEMIES row.
- `README.md` — §Gym Index Entry Scene: ENEMIES column roster is `Fodder Enemies`, `Boss`;
  the Centipede lives in the fodder gym's dropdown.

## Related work
## Related work

- **Boss appears in both lists on index screen (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X)** — established the
  precedent: exclude an enemy scene from the plain-scene column and surface a dedicated
  ENEMIES row that boots the scene directly.
- **Single enemy gym scene with in-panel enemy selector dropdown (AH-0MV13G5EV008D41E)** —
  defines the three-column index layout and the ENEMIES column semantics.
- **Centipede segmented chain (AH-0MV01EJ92008ZZ86)** — created the `GymCentipede` scene.
- **Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL)** —
  sibling categorisation pattern (Dev Utilities column owns tooling scenes).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCNZ7DN0049K73** – Scene-level tests: GymPowerUps via gameHarness (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)
- **AH-0MV2XDEKN0031KX4** – Test: gym parity intact (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: archetype, centipede, column, gym, scene (+34 more)
- `README.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, enemies (+33 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: appears, archetype, centipede, column, currently (+30 more)

Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MV4ZOIZR0086T66.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (revised by producer review):** "should be an enemy" means the Centipede
  should be reachable **inside** the enemies gym — surfaced as a dedicated **option in the
  `GymFodderEnemies` in-panel enemy selector**, which boots the same shared linked-chain code
  — rather than as a separate index entry *or* a CSV fodder config (the Centipede is a wave
  opt-in, not a CSV row). The producer rejected the dedicated ENEMIES row in review
  (2026-10-14).
- **Risk: Low.** A categorisation + dropdown-surface change with shared-code extraction; no
  gameplay, entity or spawn behaviour changes. The dedicated `GymCentipede` scene is
  unchanged in behaviour and keeps its parity tests.
- **Failure mode:** a `Centipede` label present on the index at all would make the
  `findTextAt` label lookups ambiguous — resolved by keeping `GymCentipede` out of every
  index column; it is only reachable through the fodder gym's dropdown.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general "auto-route every enemy gym scene to the ENEMIES column"
  mechanism is out of scope here; if wanted it should be captured as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No clarifying questions were required.** Research summary: the seed intent, combined
  with the existing `GymBoss` precedent (AH-0MUAYB28C004KK7X) and the documented three-column
  index contract (`src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  §"Gym surface", `README.md` §"Gym Index Entry Scene"), was sufficient to draft a clear
  brief. The one interpretation choice (dedicated ENEMIES **scene** row that boots
  `GymCentipede` directly, rather than adding a fodder-dropdown config) is recorded as an
  explicit documented assumption under Risks & assumptions.
data.title: Centipede appears in the plain scenes column instead of ENEMIES

# Shared bullet-shape rendering seam

Child of AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE (Variety in weapon graphics). The data-driven rendering seam that lets each weapon id and enemy archetype resolve its own code-drawn projectile shape(s), VFX config and feel, consumed identically by `PlayerBullet` and `bulletUtils` in the game and every gym. Most weapon children depend on this.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want one shared, parity-safe shape resolver so per-weapon and per-archetype bullet visuals live in a single seam the game and every gym consume identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Every player weapon is visually unique in flight.** Each of the 11 catalogue weapons (`cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova, mortar, arc`) has a distinct code-drawn projectile shape and/or per-shot VFX that differs from every other weapon; a doc/roster test asserts catalogue-wide uniqueness. The Wave Laser (and Dual) must render as a line/beam, **not** a dot.
- **Every enemy attack has its own projectile identity.** One child per enemy weapon (Scout/Invader aimed shot, Diver spread burst, Tank radial, Phaser radial, Swarm burst, Raider shot, Boss spread, Boss spiral, Boss pulse, Boss desperation, Capturer tractor beam, Orbital-Strike falling shell) — each with a distinct shape/colour/feel reflecting its archetype and gated by its existing fire behaviour (visuals/feel only; firing logic, speeds, intervals and patterns unchanged).
- A shape resolver exists that draws into a Phaser `Graphics` context from visual metadata and supports at least: disc, line/beam, teardrop/streak, missile, ring, shell, jagged bolt; `BulletShape` in `src/utils/weapons.ts` extends beyond `'circle' | 'line'`, and `weaponLevels.ts` carries the new fields through level resolution without changing upgrade values.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Every gameplay-visual change is applied through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, shared entities/utils) and consumed identically by the relevant gym scene(s) and `PlayScene`; the repo duplicate-body guard and gym-parity assertions must pass unchanged. No behaviour/balance re-tuning (fire rates, beat grid, speeds, damage, ranges stay as-is).
- Per-shot VFX stay cheap: small Graphics primitives, short lifetimes, reusing `src/vfx/` conventions.
- **Full test suite passes** with the new changes, including updated graphics command-buffer tests and new per-weapon visual/audio tests.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — per-shape rendering driven by weapon definition
- `src/entities/bulletUtils.ts` — shared enemy-bullet creation; per-archetype shape seam
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — extend `BulletShape`/`WeaponDefinition` with visual metadata
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — carry visual fields through level resolution
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact hooks
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `GymFodderEnemies.ts`, `GymBoss.ts` — adopt the shared seam (parity)

## Dependencies

- Parent: AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE
- Prerequisite for every weapon/attack child.

## Scope guard

Seam/infrastructure only; register signature look-ups, do not re-tune any weapon behaviour.

# Intake Brief — Make the level/wave banner background semi-transparent and extend its duration

## Problem statement

The centred level/wave announcement banner has an opaque black background, so
during the brief pause **between levels/waves it hides the action on screen**
(carried-over asteroids keep moving, enemies are still alive). Players cannot
see what is happening behind the banner. The banner also clears too quickly to
read comfortably.

## Users

- **Player** — *"As a player, I want the level/wave banner to let me see the
  field behind it while I read the announcement, and to stay on screen long
  enough to read."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The level/wave banner background is **60 % opaque** (alpha ≈ `0.6`) instead
   of fully opaque, for both the level-start announcement and the
   wave-transition banner.
2. The banner stays visible for **3.5 s** (current 1.5 s + 2 s) for both the
   level-start announcement and the wave-transition banner, then hides
   automatically as before.
3. Both the background alpha and the duration are exported constants (e.g.
   `BANNER_BACKGROUND_ALPHA`, `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS`) so tests can pin
   them.
4. Existing tests that assert the old 1.5–2 s hide timing
   (`AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN AC1/AC2`, `AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV AC6`) are updated to
   the new 3.5 s window, and a test asserts the semi-transparent background.
5. GDD §3 (level-progression transient-banner wording) is updated to the new
   3.5 s window; the constant's doc comment no longer claims the ~1.5–2 s
   requirement.
6. The full project test suite passes with the changes (no dead
   constants/parameters left behind).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity:** the banner exists **only** in `PlayScene` (no gym
  renders it), so no gym-scene change is required.
- **Readability:** the semi-transparent background must keep the white banner
  text legible against gameplay; at 60 % the existing 34 px monospace text with
  `padding {x: 20, y: 12}` is unchanged.
- The banner must remain **transient** — it still expires on its own (just
  after 3.5 s), per the GDD's "transient transitions" principle
  (AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN).
- Phaser `TextStyle.backgroundColor` takes a CSS colour string; alpha must be
  expressed as `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` (verify it renders in Phaser 4.2.1 — if
  unsupported in the canvas fill path, use `setBackgroundColor('rgba(...)')`
  or a `Graphics` rectangle behind the text).

## Existing state

- `BANNER_STYLE` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:338`) sets
  `backgroundColor: '#000000'` — fully opaque.
- `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS = 1.5` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:301`); its doc
  comment says the value "must be within the ~1.5–2 s window required by
  AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN" — this changes to 3.5 s.
- The level-start announcement (`_announceLevel`) and the wave-transition
  banner (`_updateTransitionBanner`) both call the shared `_showBanner`, so a
  single duration/alpha change covers both surfaces.

## Desired change

- Set `backgroundColor: 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)'` in `BANNER_STYLE` (or the
  equivalent alpha-based background) so the field remains visible.
- Raise `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` to `3.5` and update its doc comment to drop
  the old ~1.5–2 s constraint.
- Update the existing banner-timing tests to the new window and add a test
  pinning the semi-transparent background.
- Update GDD §3 wording for the new banner window.

## Acceptance-criteria coverage of existing tests

The following existing tests hard-code the old 2 s hide window and must be
updated with this change:
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` `AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN AC1` (`tick(2.0)` →
  hidden) and `AC2` (reappears + hides again).
- `AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV AC6` "level-name banner remains transient" (`tick` at
  2 s / 2 s + 0.5 s expect visible-then-hidden).

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `BANNER_STYLE` background and
  `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` (+ doc comment).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — update banner-timing tests; add
  semi-transparent-background assertion.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §3 transient-banner wording for the new
  3.5 s window.

## Related work

- AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN — "Level transition banner persists for the whole wave"
  (established the transient ~1.5–2 s hide behaviour this item extends).
- AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV — "Show the level name in the level-start banner"
  (banner content/transience tests this item must keep passing).
- AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2 — "Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K'"
  (established the banner label text).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** – Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K' (completed)
- **AH-0MU7JTEMC006QPSN** – Level transition banner persists for the whole wave (completed)
- **AH-0MUMMBRCC0093MGV** – Show the level name in the level-start banner (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: also, background, banner, hard, level (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: also, banner, hard, level, levels (+9 more)
- `README.md` — matched: also, background, hard, level, levels (+9 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "visible for 2 seconds longer" means the current 1.5 s
  duration is increased **to 3.5 s** (1.5 + 2). If the intent was a 2 s total,
  only the constant and GDD wording change — flag before implementation.
- **Risk (medium):** Phaser 4.2.1 `TextStyle.backgroundColor` support for
  `rgba()` CSS strings must be verified; fallback is a `Graphics` rectangle
  behind the text or `setBackgroundColor('rgba(0,0,0,0.6)')`. Covered by the
  automated background assertion in AC4.
- **Risk (low):** extending the banner window to 3.5 s lengthens the time the
  centred text covers the playfield; the 60 % transparency (not full removal)
  keeps the field visible while retaining the GDD "transient" principle.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no follow-up opportunities were observed during
  intake; if a larger banner redesign (animation, fade, resizing) is requested
  later, it should be tracked as a separate work item, not folded in here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How transparent should the banner background be?" — Answer
  (operator): "60 % opacity". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Should the +2 s apply to both the level-start announcement and the
  wave-transition banner?" — Answer (operator): "Both". Source: interactive
  reply. Note: both surfaces share `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS` via `_showBanner`,
  so a single constant change covers both.
- Q3: "How should the GDD §3 '~1.5–2 s transient' wording be handled?" —
  Answer (operator): "Update GDD". Source: interactive reply.
- Research summary: inspected `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`BANNER_STYLE`,
  `BANNER_DURATION_SECONDS`, `_showBanner`) and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
  banner tests; `wl search "banner"` surfaced the related items above. No gym
  scene renders the banner (gym-parity check performed). Phaser version is
  4.2.1; `rgba()` in `TextStyle.backgroundColor` to be verified at
  implementation time (constraint noted).
data.title: Make the background of the level/wave banner semi-transparent
